title: Semiclassical asymptotics of multiphotonic scattering probabilities with partial indistinguishability
authors: Alonso Botero, Hubert de Guise, Orlando Melo-Vargas
abstract: We propose a framework for computing multiphotonic scattering probabilities in a lossless multiport interferometer for arbitrary photon numbers and degrees of indistinguishability. By exploiting a toroidal expansion of multiphotonic states in tensor powers of single-particle states, the framework defines a map from a torus of relative phases to the probability simplex that governs the asymptotic behavior of scattering probabilities in the large-photon limit. Specifically, the probabilities concentrate on the "classically allowed region" defined by the map, and the slowly-varying part of the multiphotonic distribution reproduces a classical measure induced by the map. As a result, we are able to establish a new asymptotic formula for the multiphotonic probabilities in a general scenario of partially indistinguishable photons, while also providing a single-particle picture to explain the asymptotics of known multiphotonic transition amplitudes in the fully indistinguishable case. More broadly, our framework yields new, directly testable consequences in relation to asymptotic photon bunching patterns: it translates features of the classical map -- such as caustics and voids -- into direct predictions about regions of large or exponentially suppressed photon-distribution probability.
summary: This theoretical paper develops a framework to calculate the asymptotic behavior of multiphotonic scattering probabilities in interferometers where photons are partially indistinguishable. By mapping the problem onto a classical phase space, the authors predict that the probability distribution will concentrate on a geometrically defined 'classically allowed region.' This provides new insights into quantum interference patterns observable in photon experiments.
main_problem: The paper addresses computing the semiclassical asymptotics of multiphotonic scattering probabilities when photons exhibit partial indistinguishability.
main_result: A new asymptotic formula is established showing that these probabilities concentrate on a 'classically allowed region' defined by a classical map derived from the system's phase space.
method: The authors employ a toroidal expansion of multiphotonic states in tensor powers, leading to an integral representation whose large-photon limit is governed by a classical map.
model_or_system: The physical system is a lossless multiport interferometer analyzed using correlated mode states $|\mathbf{n}, \Gammaangle$. The model incorporates both port degrees of freedom and internal overlaps characterized by the Gram matrix $\Gamma$.
key_observables: Multiphotonic scattering probability $P(\mathbf{n}'|\mathcal{U}, \mathbf{n}, \Gamma)$, which is analyzed on the output occupation simplex.
important_parameters: The degree of indistinguishability, controlled by the Gram matrix $\Gamma$; the large-photon limit ($N 	o \infty$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the toroidal expansion and asymptotic approximations in the large-photon limit; specific mathematical identities are used to simplify determinants.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup, the occupation simplex, and crucially, visualize predicted structures like caustics (ridges of enhanced probability) and voids (regions of suppressed probability) arising from the classical map.
paper_structure: The paper moves from defining exact Fock-space expressions for scattering probabilities to developing a mathematically tractable framework using tensor power expansions. This leads to an integral representation, which is then analyzed asymptotically via complex phase variables and determinant calculations.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful tools to connect quantum interference phenomena (like photon bunching) directly to classical geometric structures (caustics/voids), offering testable predictions for quantum optics experiments.
